Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

as long as conjunction

the whole time that

also so long as (the time), while (the whole time)

classical

Sen. Ep. 76.3: tamdiū discendum est quamdiū nesciās

quamdiū

relative adverb, with the indicative; answered by tamdiū

The two actions last the same time.

Other words

  • dum — as long as, while

    conjunction, with the indicative · also used · classical · Plaut. Persa 113: Dum māne est, omnīs ēsse mortālīs decet.; Ov. Met. 2.89: dum rēsque sinit, tua corrige vōta

    For the shorter “while”, during which something else happens, see while.

  • quoad — as long as

    conjunction, with the indicative · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 15.23.1: quoad erit integrum (Lewis & Short)

  • dōnec — as long as

    conjunction, with the indicative · also used · classical · Ov. Tr. 1.9.5: dōnec eris sōspes, multōs numerābis amīcōs

    In this sense ante-classical, poetic and post-Augustan; Cicero has dōnec only for “until” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • tamdiū discendum est quamdiū nesciās; sī prōverbiō crēdimus, quamdiū vīvās

    one must learn as long as one does not know; and, if we believe the proverb, as long as one livesSen. Ep. 76.3

  • Dum māne est, omnīs ēsse mortālīs decet.

    As long as it is morning, every mortal ought to eat.Plaut. Persa 113

  • nāte, cavē, dum rēsque sinit, tua corrige vōta

    take care, my son, and change your wish while there is still timeOv. Met. 2.89

  • dōnec eris sōspes, multōs numerābis amīcōs

    as long as you do well, you will count many friendsOv. Tr. 1.9.5

See also while, until, as long as.

SourcesLewis & Short: quamdiu · Lewis & Short: dum · Lewis & Short: quoad · Lewis & Short: donec

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
